# Life OS — Design Philosophy

The product must follow a strict dark-minimalist design philosophy.

## Core principle
Show less. Reveal more when needed.

The default interface must be abstract, calm and uncluttered. Never expose every detail on one screen.

## Visual identity
- Near-black and charcoal surfaces.
- Muted white and grey typography.
- Restrained accent color.
- Premium, modern, understated aesthetic.
- Generous negative space.
- Subtle transitions and interactions.
- Create an original visual identity, not a clone of another productivity application.

## Progressive disclosure
- Default views show summaries, not full records.
- Hover reveals contextual actions on desktop.
- Click opens detailed information.
- Expandable panels reveal secondary information.
- Mobile uses tap-based interactions.
- Keep advanced controls out of the default view.

## Modularity
- Build independent, reusable components.
- Keep modules isolated and maintainable.
- Support optional modules and configurable dashboards.
- Avoid hardcoded layouts and duplicated components.
- Keep visual behavior consistent throughout the application.

## UX restrictions
- Avoid information overload.
- Avoid unnecessary cards, charts, borders and badges.
- Avoid excessive gradients and animations.
- Never add visual elements without a functional purpose.
- Prioritize readability, speed and simplicity.

Every new feature must follow these rules.
